title: Scope: Brute-Force Candidate C1, Not Scarf's Algorithm
content: The header sets the honest scope of this file. It is Candidate C1 of the `sperner-simplicial-instance-oq-05` dossier: a `Decidable`-driven brute-force witness extractor for a panchromatic cell. Two caveats are essential for a reader: (1) this is **not** Scarf's algorithm — it enumerates all cells in $O(|T.\text{Cell}|)$ rather than walking door-paths in $O(\text{path length})$; the Scarf pivot is the separate Candidate C2; (2) it does **not** yet replace the `axiom scarf_approx_fixed_point` in `BrouwerFixedPointOQ04OQ04.lean`. The mathematical content is deliberately shallow: every step is forced by pre-existing `Triangulation.cellFintype` and `CellComplex.decidableIsPanchromatic` instances. The value is naming a computable witness `def` plus a totality theorem grounded in `Triangulation.sperner`. Imports `Proofs.SpernerSimplicialInstance`; opens `CellComplex Triangulation Finset`.
mathContext: Sperner's lemma guarantees a panchromatic (fully-coloured) cell exists for any Sperner colouring; this file *extracts* one computably. Brute force $O(|T.\text{Cell}|)$ vs. Scarf pivot $O(\text{door-path length})$.

title: findPanchromaticBrute: Decidable-Driven Witness Extractor
content:
`def findPanchromaticBrute (T : Triangulation V n) (c : V → Fin (n+1)) : Option T.Cell := (Finset.univ.filter (fun s : T.Cell => IsPanchromatic c T.toCellComplex s)).toList.head?`

Fully computable; uses no `Classical.choose`. Returns `some s` if any panchromatic cell exists in `T.cellFintype.elems.toList` order, `none` otherwise. The order is implementation-specific; downstream consumers should use the `_isSome_iff` characterisation rather than rely on a specific order.
mathContext: The Option-valued brute-force finder. Domain: a pseudomanifold triangulation `T` with `[DecidableEq V]` (so `T.Cell` inherits a `Fintype` instance from `Triangulation.cellFintype` in `SpernerSimplicialInstance.lean`). Codomain: `Option T.Cell` — the `Option` wrapper is necessary because non-Sperner colourings may not produce a panchromatic cell. The `Finset.filter` is decidable via `CellComplex.decidableIsPanchromatic` (from `SpernerMathlib4.lean`), which inspects the colour-of-vertex map for surjectivity.

title: findPanchromaticBrute_isSome_iff: Membership Characterisation
content:
`theorem findPanchromaticBrute_isSome_iff (T : Triangulation V n) (c : V → Fin (n + 1)) : (findPanchromaticBrute T c).isSome ↔ ∃ s : T.Cell, IsPanchromatic c T.toCellComplex s`

Forward direction: `head? = some _` ⇒ `toList ≠ []` ⇒ Finset non-empty (`Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty`) ⇒ ∃ filter-member ⇒ ∃ panchromatic (`Finset.mem_filter`).

Backward direction: witness `s` ⇒ `s ∈ filter` (`Finset.mem_filter.2`) ⇒ Finset non-empty ⇒ `toList ≠ []` (`Finset.Nonempty.toList_ne_nil`) ⇒ `head? = some _` by case analysis on the `toList`.
mathContext: The characterisation lemma is the API entry point. The iff form means downstream consumers can pass `findPanchromaticBrute T c` through `Option.isSome` to test existence both ways. The proof uses verified Mathlib names from the lockfile-pinned v4.26.0 SHA `2df2f015...`: `Finset.toList_eq_nil` (Mathlib/Data/Finset/Basic.lean:512), `Finset.Nonempty.toList_ne_nil` (Mathlib/Data/Finset/Basic.lean:521), `Finset.nonempty_iff_ne_empty` (Mathlib/Data/Finset/Empty.lean:148).

title: findPanchromaticBrute_eq_some_imp_panchromatic: Witness Extraction
content:
`theorem findPanchromaticBrute_eq_some_imp_panchromatic (T : Triangulation V n) (c : V → Fin (n + 1)) (s : T.Cell) (heq : findPanchromaticBrute T c = some s) : IsPanchromatic c T.toCellComplex s`

From `findPanchromaticBrute T c = some s`, conclude that `s` is in fact panchromatic. The returned `s` is `List.head?` of the filtered Finset's `toList`, so by `List.mem_of_head?` it is a list-member, hence (by `Finset.mem_toList`) a filter-member, hence (by `Finset.mem_filter.2`) panchromatic.
mathContext: The strong-form witness lemma: `some s` carries a *proof* that `s` is panchromatic, not just an existence claim. Downstream consumers can `Option.get`-then-prove without re-running the filter. Combined with the `_isSome_iff` characterisation, the API is: `(findPanchromaticBrute T c).get : T.Cell` gives a witness, and `_eq_some_imp_panchromatic` gives its proof property.

title: findPanchromaticBrute_isSome_of_boundary_odd: Totality under Sperner Hypothesis
content:
`theorem findPanchromaticBrute_isSome_of_boundary_odd (T : Triangulation V n) (c : V → Fin (n + 1)) (hbdry : Odd (Finset.univ.filter (fun p : T.Cell × Fin (n + 1) => IsDoor c T.toCellComplex p.1 p.2 ∧ T.adj p.1 p.2 = none)).card) : (findPanchromaticBrute T c).isSome`

One-line proof: `by rw [findPanchromaticBrute_isSome_iff]; exact Triangulation.sperner T c hbdry`. The characterisation iff converts the goal to ∃ panchromatic, which is exactly the statement of `Triangulation.sperner`.
mathContext: Totality under the standard Sperner hypothesis: this is the use-case for `findPanchromaticBrute` — given a Sperner-coloured triangulation (boundary doors odd, which is the standard Sperner hypothesis), the finder is guaranteed to return a cell. The full pipeline is: SpernerColoring → boundary_doors_odd (from parent file) → findPanchromaticBrute_isSome_of_boundary_odd → `some s`. The classical Sperner-lemma statement says "a panchromatic cell exists"; this theorem upgrades that to "the brute-force finder finds one".

title: 1-D Demo: Panchromatic Cell on intervalTriangulation 3
content:
`example : ∃ s : Fin 3, CellComplex.IsPanchromatic (fun n : ℕ => if n ≤ 1 then (0 : Fin 2) else 1) (Triangulation.intervalTriangulation 3 (by norm_num)).toCellComplex s := by refine ⟨1, ?_⟩; decide`

On `intervalTriangulation 3` with the colouring `c(n) = if n ≤ 1 then 0 else 1`:
- Cell 0 has vertices {0, 1} → both colour 0 → NOT panchromatic
- Cell 1 has vertices {1, 2} → colours {0, 1} → **panchromatic** ✓
- Cell 2 has vertices {2, 3} → both colour 1 → NOT panchromatic

Witness: cell index 1. `decide` evaluates the `IsPanchromatic` predicate to `True` via the `CellComplex.decidableIsPanchromatic` instance — a kernel-level proof object, not just runtime evaluation.
mathContext: The demo verifies the entire C1 pipeline end-to-end on a concrete computable instance. The interval triangulation subdivides [0, 3] into 3 unit segments; the colouring puts vertices {0, 1} at colour 0 and {2, 3} at colour 1. The middle segment {1, 2} crosses the colour boundary and is therefore panchromatic — exactly what Sperner's lemma predicts for the 1-d standard simplex with a boundary-condition colouring. `decide` (kernel-level) is preferred over `#eval` (runtime-only) because it provides a proof obligation, not just a printed value.
